title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 109
paragraphs: Having crossed the dry bed of the river Lisus, he passed the Greek cities of Maroneia, Dicaea, and Abdera. These he passed by, along with the following notable lakes lying near them: the Ismarian lake, between Maroneia and Stryme; the Bistonian lake near Dicaea, into which two rivers, the Travus and the Compsatus, pour their waters. At Abdera he passed no noteworthy lake, but did pass the river Nestus, which there flows into the sea. Then, beyond these places, he went past cities of the mainland; near one of them happens to lie a lake about thirty stades in circumference, full of fish and very brackish, which the baggage animals alone drank dry by watering there. The name of this city is Pistyros.
